title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Q is an abstract square with vertices S and sides A. D = Aut(Q) is dihedral of order 8, and its centre {1, ε} is the antipodism. R = Rep(Q) is the set of 8 frames (repères) (s, a), with s a vertex and a a side through s. D acts simply transitively on R, and Rep(Q) ≅ Rep(Q°) for the dual square, where vertices and sides are exchanged. The quotient R/antipodism has 4 elements and is identified with C × D, where C = {the two axes / pairs of opposite sides} and D = {the two diagonals}. ω_Q = {R+, R−} is the 2-element set of orientations, i.e. the two classes of frames. All three of C, D, ω_Q are 2-element sets, i.e. Z/2-torsors.

On the previous page Grothendieck sets conventions embedding these sets into D:
- c ↦ the reflection in the transverse axis;
- d ↦ the reflection in the diagonal;
- an orientation given by a frame (s, a) ↦ (this page, first figure) the quarter-turn taking s to the other endpoint of a. This lands in the two elements of order 4, inside D⁺ = C4.

He then checks that with these conventions the relation ϖ·c·d = 1 in D (the quarter-turn is the product of two reflections in an axis and a diagonal) is equivalent to the following: the orientation class R_ϖ ⊂ R contains the inverse image, under R → R/a, of the element (c, d) of R/a ≅ C × D. In other words, it gives an explicit trivialisation ω_Q ⊗ C ⊗ D ≅ 1 of the product of the three Z/2-torsors. This corresponds to the fact that the three nontrivial characters of D_ab ≅ (Z/2)² multiply to the trivial character.

He then explains an apparent paradox. Writing the relation through the dual square Q° seems to give the opposite sign. The reason is that the identification Rep(Q) = Rep(Q°), compatible with Aut Q = Aut Q° (which, he stresses, can reasonably be made in only one way and is not a matter of convention), sends an orientation class of frames to opposite orientations of Q and Q°. The rotation s → s' and the rotation a → a' attached to the same frame (s, a) are mutually inverse (second figure).

Purpose: sign and convention bookkeeping for the dihedral group that appears in the level-2 / Legendre-type description of moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2. The next page analyses Aut D as W ⋊ ±1, with the structure (c, d) cutting it down to inner automorphisms.
errors: No mathematical error. The apparent sign reversal under passing to the dual square is correctly explained by the frame identification reversing orientation; it is a convention subtlety, not a mistake.

ideas.what: Orientations, axis-pairs and diagonals of a square are three Z/2-torsors whose tensor product is canonically trivial (ϖ c d = 1), made explicit via frames modulo antipodism.
ideas.modern_name: Product of the three nontrivial characters of D8^ab ≅ (Z/2)^2 is trivial; trivialisation of a tensor product of μ2-torsors

ideas.what: The canonical identification Rep(Q) ≅ Rep(Q°) for the dual square reverses orientation: the rotations s→s' and a→a' attached to a frame are opposite.
ideas.modern_name: Orientation reversal under duality of a regular polygon (flag set of a polygon and its dual)

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but elementary sign-convention bookkeeping about the dihedral group of the square and three 2-element torsors. It is typical of Grothendieck's style of checking canonicity, but there is no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely 'je lui associe la rotation du carré qui transforme s en le deuxième sommet de a' (not 'je laisse vérifier la relation des coin par transformer').
'R → R/=' and '(c,d) de R/=' should read R/a (underlined a = antipodism).
'par le coin dual' should be 'par le carré dual'.
'à l'une des régions de Q et de Q°' should likely be 'à l'ensemble des repères de Q et de Q°'.
'ce qui n'est possible conséquence que d'un seul geste' is likely 'ce qui n'est possible raisonnablement que d'une seule façon'.
'dans une classe Q' dans R' is likely 'alors une classe R' dans R ... considérée comme définissant'.
'des relations qu'il définit' and 'deux relations opposées' should be 'des rotations' and 'deux rotations opposées'.
